stations.title: Anterior STEMI — ECG Interpretation
stations.task: Interpret the 12-lead ECG and discuss the management of a patient with acute chest pain

dataPresented.scenario: A 62-year-old man presents to the ED with crushing central chest pain radiating to the left arm for 45 minutes, associated with diaphoresis and nausea. He is haemodynamically stable. Here is the 12-lead ECG obtained on arrival.

images.title: 12-lead ECG
images.alt: 12-lead ECG showing ST elevation in V1-V4 with reciprocal ST depression in II, III and aVF
images.caption: 12-lead ECG — anterior leads V1-V4 show marked ST elevation with reciprocal changes in the inferior leads.

keySymptoms: Crushing central chest pain radiating to left arm
ST elevation in V1-V4 on ECG
redFlags: Reciprocal ST depression in inferior leads
Onset within 45 minutes — within reperfusion window

mustAsk: Localize the ST elevation to the anterior leads (V1-V4)
bonus: State the reperfusion goal (PCI within 90 minutes / fibrinolysis within 30)

questions.question: Describe the ECG findings. What is your diagnosis?
questions.answer: ST elevation in V1-V4 with reciprocal ST depression in II, III and aVF — acute anterior ST-elevation MI.
questions.rubric: Correctly interprets ST elevation location and reciprocal changes

questions.question: Which coronary artery is most likely the culprit?
How would you manage this patient in the first 10 minutes?
questions.answer: Activate the cath lab (primary PCI within 90 minutes), loading dose of dual antiplatelet therapy, anticoagulation (heparin), morphine for pain if needed, monitor for arrhythmias.
questions.rubric: Covers reperfusion pathway, antiplatelets and anticoagulation

stations.title: Right Lower Lobe Pneumonia — CXR
stations.task: Interpret the chest X-ray and manage a patient with community-acquired pneumonia

dataPresented.scenario: A 58-year-old woman presents with a cough productive of purulent sputum for 4 days, fever of 38.4°C and right-sided pleuritic chest pain. She is not short of breath at rest. Here is her chest X-ray.

images.title: Chest X-ray (PA)
images.alt: PA chest X-ray showing dense right lower zone opacity with air bronchograms, silhouetting the right hemidiaphragm
images.caption: PA CXR — dense consolidation in the right lower zone with air bronchograms and an obscured right hemidiaphragm (silhouette sign).

keySymptoms: Purulent sputum, fever, pleuritic chest pain
Right lower zone consolidation on CXR
hiddenProfile.vitalSigns: BP 126/78, HR 98, RR 22, O2 sat 94% on air, Temp 38.4°C

mustAsk: Localize the opacity to the right lower lobe

questions.question: Describe the CXR findings. What is the diagnosis?
questions.answer: Dense opacity in the right lower zone with air bronchograms and an obscured right hemidiaphragm — right lower lobe consolidation, consistent with lobar pneumonia.
questions.rubric: Recognizes consolidation, air bronchograms and silhouette sign

questions.question: What is the most likely causative organism?
questions.answer: Streptococcus pneumoniae — typical community-acquired pneumonia in this setting.
questions.rubric: Names S. pneumoniae as most likely organism

questions.question: How would you manage this patient?
questions.answer: Assess severity with CURB-65, start empiric oral antibiotics (amoxicillin, or doxycycline in penicillin allergy), analgesia, and review with safety-netting for deterioration.
questions.rubric: Covers severity assessment and appropriate empiric antibiotics

stations.title: Intracerebral Haemorrhage — CT Head
stations.task: Interpret the CT head and manage an anticoagulated patient with a suspected stroke

dataPresented.scenario: A 70-year-old man on warfarin for atrial fibrillation presents with a sudden severe headache and left-sided weakness that started 2 hours ago. GCS 13. Here is his non-contrast CT head.

images.title: CT Head (axial, non-contrast)
images.alt: Axial CT head showing a hyperdense haematoma in the right basal ganglia with surrounding oedema
images.caption: Non-contrast CT head — a large hyperdense haematoma in the right basal ganglia with perihaematomal oedema, in keeping with primary intracerebral haemorrhage.

mustAsk: Recognize the hyperdense haematoma in the right basal ganglia
Identify the urgency of anticoagulation reversal
bonus: Discuss INR targets and repeat imaging

questions.question: Describe the CT findings. What is the diagnosis?
questions.answer: A large hyperdense haematoma in the right basal ganglia with surrounding oedema — spontaneous intracerebral haemorrhage.

questions.question: What is the single most urgent intervention?
questions.answer: Reverse the warfarin immediately — intravenous vitamin K and prothrombin complex concentrate (PCC).
questions.rubric: Names anticoagulation reversal as the priority

questions.question: What are the key ongoing management priorities?
questions.answer: Blood pressure control, repeat imaging for haematoma expansion, neurosurgery assessment, and monitoring for neurological deterioration.
questions.rubric: Covers BP control, repeat imaging and neurosurgery assessment

stations.title: CKD with Hyperkalaemia — Laboratory Report
stations.task: Interpret the renal function panel and manage a patient with chronic kidney disease and hyperkalaemia

dataPresented.scenario: A 66-year-old man with type 2 diabetes and hypertension for 15 years presents with progressive fatigue, ankle swelling and reduced urine output. Here is his renal function panel.

images.title: Renal Function Panel
images.alt: Lab report showing creatinine 3.2, eGFR 24, potassium 6.1, bicarbonate 18 and elevated urea
images.caption: Renal function panel — creatinine 3.2 mg/dL, eGFR 24, potassium 6.1 mmol/L (H), bicarbonate 18 (L), urea 68 (H), phosphate 5.9 (H).

hiddenProfile.diagnosis: Stage 4 chronic kidney disease with hyperkalaemia and metabolic acidosis (chronic diabetic nephropathy)
keySymptoms: Fatigue, ankle oedema, reduced urine output

mustAsk: Recognize the CKD stage and severity
Identify hyperkalaemia as the urgent finding
Discuss ECG first, then treatment of hyperkalaemia

questions.question: Interpret this renal function panel. What is the stage of kidney disease?
questions.answer: Creatinine 3.2 with eGFR 24 — stage 4 CKD (G4) with hyperkalaemia, metabolic acidosis and hyperphosphataemia.
questions.rubric: Interprets eGFR and stages CKD correctly

questions.question: What is the most urgent abnormality to address and why?
questions.answer: Hyperkalaemia (K 6.1) — risk of life-threatening cardiac arrhythmia. An ECG should be performed immediately.
questions.rubric: Identifies hyperkalaemia as the urgent finding and its cardiac risk

questions.question: How would you manage the hyperkalaemia?
questions.answer: Calcium gluconate for cardiac protection, insulin-dextrose and/or nebulised salbutamol to shift potassium intracellularly, then enhance elimination and review the cause; assess for dialysis if refractory or oliguric.
questions.rubric: Covers cardiac protection and potassium shift therapies
